subproblems.title: Properness transfers to uniformly close continuous maps and to their affine homotopy on the cylinder (supplied fact (P))
subproblems.statement: Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p. A map g : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} is proper on F ⊆ ℝ^m if g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m′}. For y ∈ ℝ^{m+1} let t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)), and for F ⊆ ℝ^m let cyl(F) := {y ∈ ℝ^{m+1} : t(y) ∈ [0,1] and tl(y) ∈ F}. (a) For all m, m′ ∈ ℕ, maps G, g : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, every closed F ⊆ ℝ^m and every d ∈ ℝ: if g is continuous, G is proper on F and dist(g(x), G(x)) ≤ d for every x ∈ F, then g is proper on F. (b) For all m, m′ ∈ ℕ, maps G, F₀, F₁ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, every closed F ⊆ ℝ^m and every d ∈ ℝ: if F₀ and F₁ are continuous, G is proper on F, and dist(F₀(x), G(x)) ≤ d and dist(F₁(x), G(x)) ≤ d for every x ∈ F, then the affine homotopy H : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m′}, H(y) := F₀(tl(y)) + t(y)·(F₁(tl(y)) − F₀(tl(y))), is proper on cyl(F). (G itself need not be continuous.)

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: fact (P) (properness transfer) of the supplied proof of lipschitz_pushforward, with all details filled in.

1. (Preliminaries.) ℝ^{m′} is a proper metric space, so for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^{m′} and every d ∈ ℝ the closed d-neighbourhood cthickening d K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening). If u ∈ K and dist(v, u) ≤ d then v ∈ cthickening d K (mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). Compact subsets of ℝ^{m′} are closed, and a closed subset of a compact set is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
2. (Part (a).) Let K ⊆ ℝ^{m′} be compact. The set g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is closed, because g is continuous, K is closed and F is closed. If x ∈ g⁻¹(K) ∩ F, then g(x) ∈ K and dist(G(x), g(x)) = dist(g(x), G(x)) ≤ d, so G(x) ∈ cthickening d K by step 1. Hence g⁻¹(K) ∩ F ⊆ G⁻¹(cthickening d K) ∩ F, and the latter set is compact by the properness of G on F applied to the compact set cthickening d K. By step 1, g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact. So g is proper on F.
3. (Coordinates on ℝ^{m+1}.) The maps t and tl are continuous (indeed continuous linear): they are composed of the continuous linear equivalences EuclideanSpace.equiv, the evaluation at 0 and Fin.tail. For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m let cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)). The map (s, x) ↦ cons(s, x) is continuous, and cons(t(y), tl(y)) = y for every y ∈ ℝ^{m+1} (Fin.cons_self_tail).
4. (Closedness in part (b).) H is continuous, being the sum of F₀ ∘ tl and the product of the continuous scalar function t with the continuous map F₁ ∘ tl − F₀ ∘ tl. The set cyl(F) = t⁻¹([0,1]) ∩ tl⁻¹(F) is closed, since t and tl are continuous and [0,1] and F are closed. Hence, for compact (so closed) K, the set H⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(F) is closed.
5. (Part (b): a compact set containing H⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(F).) Let K be compact and K₁ := G⁻¹(cthickening d K) ∩ F, which is compact by the properness of G on F (cthickening d K is compact by step 1). Let y ∈ H⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(F), and put s := t(y) ∈ [0,1] and x := tl(y) ∈ F. Then H(y) − G(x) = (1 − s)·(F₀(x) − G(x)) + s·(F₁(x) − G(x)), hence dist(H(y), G(x)) ≤ (1 − s)·dist(F₀(x), G(x)) + s·dist(F₁(x), G(x)) ≤ (1 − s)·d + s·d = d, using 1 − s ≥ 0 and s ≥ 0. Since H(y) ∈ K, step 1 gives G(x) ∈ cthickening d K, so x ∈ K₁. By step 3, y = cons(s, x) with (s, x) ∈ [0,1] × K₁. Thus H⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(F) is contained in the image of the compact set [0,1] × K₁ under the continuous map (s, x) ↦ cons(s, x), which is compact.
6. (Conclusion of (b).) By steps 4 and 5, H⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(F) is a closed subset of a compact set, hence compact (step 1). So H is proper on cyl(F). ∎
proof_key_steps: cthickening d K is compact for compact K in the proper space ℝ^{m′}, and dist(g x, G x) ≤ d puts G(x) into it.
(a) g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is closed (g continuous, F closed) and contained in the compact G⁻¹(cthickening d K) ∩ F.
(b) For y ∈ cyl(F), H(y) − G(tl y) = (1 − t)(F₀ − G) + t(F₁ − G) at tl y, so dist(H(y), G(tl y)) ≤ d.
Hence H⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(F) ⊆ cons([0,1] × (G⁻¹(cthickening d K) ∩ F)), a compact set; H is continuous and cyl(F) closed, so the closed subset is compact.

2. (Uniform convergence to G on F_{r/2}.) Since 0 < r/2 ≤ r, F_{r/2} ⊆ F_r (thickening_mono), so Ĝ = G on F_{r/2}. Uniform convergence on ℝ^m implies uniform convergence on the subset F_{r/2} (TendstoUniformly.tendstoUniformlyOn), and since the limit Ĝ agrees with G on F_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on F_{r/2} (TendstoUniformlyOn.congr_right).
3. (Eventual closeness on F.) F ⊆ F_{r/2} because r/2 > 0 (self_subset_thickening). By step 2 and the metric characterization of uniform convergence (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff) with ε = 1, there is n₀ such that for all n ≥ n₀ and all x ∈ F_{r/2}, dist(G(x), G_n(x)) < 1; in particular dist(G_n(x), G(x)) ≤ 1 for all n ≥ n₀ and x ∈ F.
4. (Eventual properness.) Let n ≥ n₀. G_n is continuous (a C^∞ map is continuous), F is closed, G is proper on F and dist(G_n(x), G(x)) ≤ 1 on F, so part (a) of the sibling proper_transfer (with g := G_n and d := 1) shows that G_n is proper on F. Hence G_n is proper on F for all sufficiently large n, which completes the proof. ∎

Recall spt Z = U ∖ zeroRegion(Z), where zeroRegion(Z) is the union of all W with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and Z(η) = 0 for every η ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (“Z vanishes on W”). (F2′): by the reused lemma isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support, Z(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt Z = ∅. (Balls): for x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, W := B_r(x) is open, closure W = B̄_r(x) (`closure_ball`) is compact (`isCompact_closedBall`); so W is admissible for zeroRegion as soon as B̄_r(x) ⊆ U and Z vanishes on W.

1. (Part (1).) Let x ∈ spt ∂Z, so x ∈ U, and suppose x ∉ spt Z. Then x ∈ zeroRegion(Z): x ∈ W for some W open with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, and Z vanishing on W. For φ ∈ D^m(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W we have tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ W (SimonGMT `tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset`), so ∂Z(φ) = Z(dφ) = 0. Thus ∂Z vanishes on W, W is admissible for zeroRegion(∂Z), and x ∈ zeroRegion(∂Z), contradicting x ∈ spt ∂Z. Hence spt ∂Z ⊆ spt Z. (No openness of U is needed.)
2. (Part (2).) Let x ∈ spt Z ⊆ U and suppose x ∉ K. The set U ∖ K is open (U open, K closed) and contains x, so there is r > 0 with B̄_r(x) ⊆ U ∖ K (take half of a radius of a ball inside U ∖ K). Let W := B_r(x). For ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W: tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅, hence tsupport ω ∩ spt Z_j = ∅ for every j, so Z_j(ω) = 0 by (F2′); since Z_j(ω) → Z(ω) and limits in ℝ are unique, Z(ω) = 0. So Z vanishes on W, W is admissible, x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting x ∈ spt Z. Hence spt Z ⊆ K.
3. (Part (3).) Let x ∈ spt Z ⊆ U and suppose x ∉ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2. As x ∈ U, x ∈ zeroRegion(Z_1) ∩ zeroRegion(Z_2) ∩ U, an open set (zero regions are unions of open sets, U is open), so there is r > 0 with B̄_r(x) contained in it. Let W := B_r(x). For ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W: tsupport ω ⊆ zeroRegion(Z_i), which is disjoint from spt Z_i = U ∖ zeroRegion(Z_i), so Z_i(ω) = 0 by (F2′) (i = 1, 2), and Z(ω) = a·0 + b·0 = 0. So Z vanishes on W, W is admissible (B̄_r(x) ⊆ U), x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting x ∈ spt Z. Hence spt Z ⊆ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2. ∎
proof_key_steps: If Z vanishes on an admissible W then so does ∂Z, because tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ; hence spt ∂Z ⊆ spt Z.
For x ∉ K a small ball W around x misses K, so every Z_j kills test forms supported in W (reused vanishing lemma) and so does the weak limit Z.
For x outside spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2 a small ball lies in both zero regions; both Z_i, hence Z = aZ_1 + bZ_2, vanish on it.

Notation: for maps F₀, F₁ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, H[F₀, F₁](y) := F₀(tl(y)) + t(y)·(F₁(tl(y)) − F₀(tl(y))) is the affine homotopy appearing in (Aff); for a test form ψ, dψ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ _ ψ, whose underlying form is exteriorDerivative ψ; |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm. Assume (Prod) and (SH) and fix m, m′, k, X, G, (G_n), (G′_n), O, O′, L, L′, ω, (η_n), (η′_n) as in the claim.

0. (Preliminaries.)
(i) spt X = univ ∖ zeroRegion(X) is closed, the zero region being open. If k = j + 1, the HEq hypothesis applied to j and Y := X (k = j + 1, HEq X X) gives M(∂X) < ∞; moreover spt ∂X ⊆ spt X by part (1) of the reused support_lemmas (with U := univ), and spt ∂X is closed.
(ii) (Bounded test forms.) For every test form ψ on ℝ^{m′} the function y ↦ |ψ(y)| is continuous (|·| is the square root of a finite sum of squares of the evaluations α ↦ α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(q)}), each continuous linear in α, and ψ is continuous) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ψ; hence it is bounded, and there is C_ψ ≥ 0 with |ψ(y)| ≤ C_ψ for all y. Put C₁ := C_{dω} and, if k = j + 1, C₂ := C_ω.
(iii) (Products.) By (Prod) for X there is Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z). If k = j + 1, then ∂X ∈ D_j(ℝ^m) has M(∂X) < ∞, and (Prod) for ∂X gives Z′ ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(∂X, Z′).
(iv) (Constants.) (Aff) for (m, m′, k) gives c ≥ 0; if k = j + 1, (Aff) for (m, m′, j) gives c′ ≥ 0. Put O″ := O ∩ O′ (open, spt X ⊆ O″), L″ := max(max(L, L′), 0) ≥ 0 and B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0, so that M(X) = ENNReal.ofReal B because M(X) < ∞; if k = j + 1 put B′ := M(∂X).toReal ≥ 0, so M(∂X) = ENNReal.ofReal B′. Let C₀ := c·B·C₁ if k = 0 and C₀ := c·L″^{j+1}·B·C₁ + c′·L″^j·B′·C₂ if k = j + 1; then C₀ ≥ 0.
(v) (The affine homotopy.) If F₀, F₁ are C^∞, then H := H[F₀, F₁] is C^∞, because t and tl are continuous linear maps and sums, products with the C^∞ scalar function t, and compositions of C^∞ maps are C^∞. Since t(cons(s, x)) = s and tl(cons(s, x)) = x, we have H(cons(0, x)) = F₀(x) + 0 = F₀(x) and H(cons(1, x)) = F₀(x) + (F₁(x) − F₀(x)) = F₁(x) for all x; i.e. the maps x ↦ H(cons(0, x)) and x ↦ H(cons(1, x)) are F₀ and F₁ (so they also have the same derivatives).
1. (Core estimate.) Claim: let F₀, F₁ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} be C^∞ and s ≥ 0, and assume: dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ s, ‖fderiv ℝ F₀ x‖ ≤ L″ and ‖fderiv ℝ F₁ x‖ ≤ L″ for all x ∈ O″; F₀ is proper on spt X; H := H[F₀, F₁] is proper on cyl(spt X); and η₀, η₁ ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) are compatible near spt X with (F₀, ω) and (F₁, ω), respectively. Then |X(η₁) − X(η₀)| ≤ C₀·s.
Proof of the claim. By 0(v), η₀ and η₁ are compatible near spt X with (x ↦ H(cons(0, x)), ω) and (x ↦ H(cons(1, x)), ω), which is the form required in (E0) and (E1). H is C^∞ and proper on cyl(spt X), so the reused compatible_form (with P := m + 1, Q := m′, U := V := univ, A := cyl(spt X), f := H) applied to the test form dω gives η′ ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) compatible with (H, dω) near cyl(spt X), where the underlying form of dω is exteriorDerivative ω.
Case k = 0. (E0), applied to X, Z, G := H, ω, η₀, η₁ and η′, gives X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′). (Aff) for (m, m′, 0), applied to X, Z, F₀, F₁, O″, s, L″, B, ψ := dω, C := C₁ and η′ (its hypotheses are exactly: 0 ≤ s, 0 ≤ L″, 0 ≤ B, M(X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B, ProdChar(X, Z), F₀ and F₁ C^∞, O″ open with spt X ⊆ O″, the distance and derivative bounds on O″, F₀ proper on spt X, |dω(y)| ≤ C₁ for all y, and η′ compatible near cyl(spt X) with (H[F₀, F₁], dω)), gives |Z(η′)| ≤ c·s·L″^0·B·C₁ = C₀·s.
Case k = j + 1. The reused compatible_form applied to ω gives also θ′ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and an open N′ ⊇ cyl(spt X) on which θ′ is compatible with (H, ω). (E1), applied to X, Z, Z′, G := H, ω, η₀, η₁, η′ and θ′, gives X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′) + Z′(θ′). (Aff) for (m, m′, j + 1), applied to X, Z, ψ := dω, C := C₁ and η′ as in the case k = 0, gives |Z(η′)| ≤ c·s·L″^{j+1}·B·C₁. (Aff) for (m, m′, j) is applied to ∂X, Z′, F₀, F₁, O″, s, L″, B′, ψ := ω, C := C₂ and θ′: its hypotheses hold because M(∂X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B′, ProdChar(∂X, Z′) holds, spt ∂X ⊆ spt X ⊆ O″, F₀ is proper on spt ∂X (for compact K, F₀⁻¹(K) ∩ spt ∂X = (F₀⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X) ∩ spt ∂X is the intersection of a compact set with a closed set), and θ′ is compatible with (H, ω) near cyl(spt ∂X) on the same N′ (cyl(spt ∂X) ⊆ cyl(spt X)); it gives |Z′(θ′)| ≤ c′·s·L″^j·B′·C₂. Hence |X(η₁) − X(η₀)| ≤ |Z(η′)| + |Z′(θ′)| ≤ C₀·s. This proves the claim.
2. (Eventual hypotheses.) Fix ε > 0. Each of the following finitely many statements holds for all sufficiently large n, hence all of them hold simultaneously for all n ≥ some n_ε: (a) ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O and ‖fderiv ℝ G′_n x‖ ≤ L′ for all x ∈ O′ (hypotheses); (b) dist(G(x), G_n(x)) < ε for all x ∈ O and dist(G(x), G′_n(x)) < ε for all x ∈ O′ (uniform convergence, Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff); (c) η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X and η′_n is compatible with (G′_n, ω) near spt X (hypotheses).
3. (Applying the core estimate.) Let n ≥ n_ε, F₀ := G_n and F₁ := G′_n; both are C^∞, hence continuous. On O″ we have ‖fderiv ℝ F₀ x‖ ≤ L ≤ L″, ‖fderiv ℝ F₁ x‖ ≤ L′ ≤ L″ and dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ dist(F₁(x), G(x)) + dist(G(x), F₀(x)) < 2ε. On spt X ⊆ O″ we have dist(F₀(x), G(x)) ≤ ε and dist(F₁(x), G(x)) ≤ ε; since spt X is closed and G is proper on spt X, part (a) of proper_transfer (g := F₀, d := ε) shows that F₀ is proper on spt X, and part (b) of proper_transfer (d := ε) shows that H[F₀, F₁] is proper on cyl(spt X). The core estimate (step 1) with s := 2ε, η₀ := η_n and η₁ := η′_n gives |X(η′_n) − X(η_n)| ≤ 2C₀·ε.
4. (Conclusion.) Let δ > 0 and ε := δ/(2C₀ + 1) > 0. By steps 2 and 3, for all sufficiently large n, |X(η′_n) − X(η_n) − 0| ≤ 2C₀·ε = δ·2C₀/(2C₀ + 1) < δ. Hence X(η′_n) − X(η_n) → 0. ∎

Formalization remark (not part of the mathematical argument): when (E0)/(E1) and (Aff) are instantiated, take G := the explicit lambda y ↦ F₀(tl y) + t(y)·(F₁(tl y) − F₀(tl y)) exactly as written in (Aff); the endpoint identities of 0(v) are then the function equalities (x ↦ H(cons(0, x))) = F₀ and (x ↦ H(cons(1, x))) = F₁, proved by funext from t(cons(s, x)) = s and tl(cons(s, x)) = x (both hold by rfl), and the compatibility hypotheses of (E0)/(E1) follow by rewriting with them.

The affine homotopy H[F₀, F₁] is C^∞ with H(cons(0,·)) = F₀ and H(cons(1,·)) = F₁, so η₀, η₁ are compatible in the form required by (E0)/(E1).

Source: fact (F3) of the parent proof. The parent justifies (F3) by the singular value decomposition. Transferring that argument to covectorEuclideanNorm, which is defined on continuous alternating maps through the standard basis, would need an SVD factorization L = Σ_i σ_i u_i ⊗ v_i and the orthonormality, for this norm, of the wedges of an arbitrary orthonormal basis. The pinned Mathlib has singular values (LinearMap.singularValues) and an inner product on the abstract exterior power ⋀[ℝ]^n E, but neither the factorization nor any link to covectorEuclideanNorm. The same inequality is therefore proved by the elementary tensor (Hilbert–Schmidt) argument below, which uses only the standard bases.

Notation:
- e_1, …, e_P and e′_1, …, e′_Q are the standard orthonormal bases of ℝ^P and ℝ^Q (EuclideanSpace.basisFun);
- for i : Fin j → Fin P, e∘i := (e_{i(1)}, …, e_{i(j)}), and similarly e′∘i for i : Fin j → Fin Q;
- |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ, so for a j-covector γ on ℝ^m (m ∈ {P, Q}, with the corresponding standard basis), |γ|² = Σ_{I : Fin j → Fin m strictly increasing} γ(e∘I)²;
- L^#α := α.compContinuousLinearMap L, so (L^#α)(v₁, …, v_j) = α(Lv₁, …, Lv_j);
- |·| on vectors is the Euclidean norm, ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product, and ‖L‖ the operator norm.

1. (Sum over all index tuples.) For every j-covector γ on ℝ^m: Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin m} γ(e∘i)² = j!·|γ|².
   (a) If i is not injective, e∘i has two equal entries, so γ(e∘i) = 0 because γ is alternating.
   (b) The map (I, σ) ↦ I ∘ σ is a bijection from pairs (I strictly increasing Fin j → Fin m, σ a permutation of Fin j) onto the injective maps Fin j → Fin m.
      - Surjectivity: for injective i, the tuple i ∘ (sort i) is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective, hence strictly increasing. With I := i ∘ sort i and σ := (sort i)⁻¹, I ∘ σ = i.
      - Injectivity: if I ∘ σ = I′ ∘ σ′, then range I = range I′. A strictly increasing map Fin j → Fin m is determined by its range (it enumerates the range in increasing order), so I = I′, and then σ = σ′ because I is injective.
   (c) For such pairs, γ(e∘(I ∘ σ)) = sign(σ)·γ(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm), so γ(e∘(I ∘ σ))² = γ(e∘I)².
   By (a)–(c), Σ_i γ(e∘i)² = Σ_{I strictly increasing} Σ_σ γ(e∘I)² = j!·Σ_I γ(e∘I)² = j!·|γ|², because Fin j has j! permutations.
2. (One slot.) For every linear functional λ : ℝ^Q → ℝ: Σ_{a=1}^{P} λ(Le_a)² ≤ ‖L‖²·Σ_{b=1}^{Q} λ(e′_b)².
   - Put g := Σ_b λ(e′_b)e′_b ∈ ℝ^Q. Then λ(y) = ⟨g, y⟩ for every y (expand y = Σ_b ⟨e′_b, y⟩e′_b), and |g|² = Σ_b λ(e′_b)².
   - Put u := Σ_a λ(Le_a)e_a ∈ ℝ^P. Then |u|² = Σ_a λ(Le_a)², and by linearity λ(Lu) = Σ_a λ(Le_a)² = |u|².
   - By Cauchy–Schwarz, |u|² = ⟨g, Lu⟩ ≤ |g|·|Lu| ≤ |g|·‖L‖·|u|.
   Hence |u| ≤ ‖L‖·|g| (trivial if u = 0, otherwise divide by |u|), and squaring gives the claim.
3. (All slots, by induction on j.) For every j ∈ ℕ and every j-multilinear map β : (ℝ^Q)^j → ℝ:
   Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin P} β(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j)})² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin Q} β(e′∘i)².
   For j = 0 both sides equal β()², because there is exactly one empty tuple and ‖L‖⁰ = 1.
   For the step j → j + 1, write tuples as i = Fin.cons a i′ with a ∈ Fin P and i′ : Fin j → Fin P (and likewise over Fin Q). Write Le∘i′ := (Le_{i′(1)}, …, Le_{i′(j)}).
   - For fixed a, the induction hypothesis applied to the j-multilinear map β(Le_a, ·) gives Σ_{i′} β(Le_a, Le∘i′)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″ : Fin j → Fin Q} β(Le_a, e′∘i″)².
   - Summing over a, the left sides add up to Σ_{i : Fin (j+1) → Fin P} β(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j+1)})². After exchanging the finite sums, the right sides add up to ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″} Σ_a λ_{i″}(Le_a)², where λ_{i″}(y) := β(y, e′∘i″) is a linear functional on ℝ^Q.
   - By step 2, this is at most ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i″} ‖L‖²·Σ_b β(e′_b, e′∘i″)² = ‖L‖^{2(j+1)}·Σ_{i : Fin (j+1) → Fin Q} β(e′∘i)².
   This proves the claim for j + 1.
4. (Conclusion.) Apply step 3 to β := α, an alternating and in particular multilinear map. Since (L^#α)(e∘i) = α(Le_{i(1)}, …, Le_{i(j)}), this gives
   Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin P} (L^#α)(e∘i)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·Σ_{i : Fin j → Fin Q} α(e′∘i)².
   By step 1, applied to L^#α on ℝ^P and to α on ℝ^Q, this reads j!·|L^#α|² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j}·j!·|α|². Dividing by j! > 0 gives |L^#α|² ≤ (‖L‖^j·|α|)². Both |L^#α| and ‖L‖^j·|α| are nonnegative, so |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j·|α|.
   No restriction on j, P, Q is used. For j = 0 both sides equal |α()|; if j > P or j > Q, the corresponding sums over strictly increasing indices are empty. ∎
proof_key_steps: For an alternating γ, the sum of γ(e∘i)² over all index tuples equals j!·|γ|²: non-injective tuples give 0, and injective ones are uniquely permutations of increasing ones.
Single-slot bound Σ_a λ(L e_a)² ≤ ‖L‖² Σ_b λ(e′_b)², via the Riesz vector g of λ, u = Σ_a λ(Le_a)e_a and Cauchy–Schwarz.
Induction over the j slots of a multilinear map gives Σ_i α(L e∘i)² ≤ ‖L‖^{2j} Σ_i α(e′∘i)².
Divide by j! and take square roots: |L^#α| ≤ ‖L‖^j |α|.

Since tsupport η ⊆ O₀ ⊆ univ, the same form is an element η_n(ω) of D^k(ℝ^m), and it is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X (on N). Let C ∈ ℝ with |ω(y)| ≤ C for all y (so C ≥ 0). For x ∈ O₀: |η_n(ω)(x)| = ζ(x)·|ω(G_n x)∘DG_n(x)| ≤ ‖DG_n(x)‖^k·|ω(G_n x)| ≤ Λ^k·C, by step 2, 0 ≤ ζ(x) ≤ 1, the reused pullback_norm, ‖DG_n(x)‖ ≤ Λ and the monotonicity of u ↦ u^k on [0, ∞). For x ∉ O₀: x ∉ tsupport η, so η_n(ω)(x) = 0 and |η_n(ω)(x)| = 0 ≤ Λ^k·C. For n < n₀ put η_n(ω) := 0. Thus, for every ω: (a) η_n(ω) is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X for all n ≥ n₀; (b) for every C with |ω(y)| ≤ C for all y, |η_n(ω)(x)| ≤ Λ^k·C for all n and x (trivially when η_n(ω) = 0, as Λ^k·C ≥ 0).
4. (Uniform bound.) The reused mass_bound (P := m, n := k, U := W := univ, T := X, B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0, which satisfies X.massOn univ = M(X) = ENNReal.ofReal B because M(X) < ∞; tsupport ⊆ univ; C := Λ^k·C) gives |X(η_n(ω))| ≤ M(X).toReal·Λ^k·C for all n, whenever |ω(y)| ≤ C for all y.
5. (Subsequences.) If p : ℕ → ℕ tends to ∞, then the maps G_{p(i)} are C^∞, satisfy ‖fderiv ℝ G_{p(i)} x‖ ≤ Λ on O₀, and converge to G uniformly on O₀ (for every ε > 0 the statement 'dist(G(x), G_n(x)) < ε for all x ∈ O₀' holds for all large n, hence for n = p(i) for all large i); and η_{p(i)}(ω) is compatible with (G_{p(i)}, ω) near spt X as soon as p(i) ≥ n₀, i.e. for all large i.
6. (Existence of the limit.) Fix ω and let a_n := X(η_n(ω)). Claim: for all p, q : ℕ → ℕ tending to ∞, a_{q(i)} − a_{p(i)} → 0. Indeed, apply (CL) to X and G (M(X) < ∞, the HEq hypothesis, G proper on spt X), to the approximations (G_{p(i)})_i with O₀, Λ and (G_{q(i)})_i with O₀, Λ, to the form ω and to the sequences (η_{p(i)}(ω))_i and (η_{q(i)}(ω))_i; all its hypotheses hold by steps 1 and 5. Now (a_n) is a Cauchy sequence: otherwise there is ε > 0 such that for every i there are p(i), q(i) ≥ i with |a_{q(i)} − a_{p(i)}| ≥ ε; then p and q tend to ∞ while a_{q(i)} − a_{p(i)} does not tend to 0, contradicting the claim. Since ℝ is complete, (a_n) converges; let S₀(ω) := lim_n X(η_n(ω)).
7. (Linearity.) Let ω, ω′ ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}), a, b ∈ ℝ and ω″ := a·ω + b·ω′. For n ≥ n₀ the form a·η_n(ω) + b·η_n(ω′) is compatible with (G_n, ω″) near spt X: on the open set N ∩ N′ ⊇ spt X (N, N′ the open sets of step 3 for ω and ω′) its value at x is a·(ω(G_n x)∘DG_n(x)) + b·(ω′(G_n x)∘DG_n(x)) = (a·ω(G_n x) + b·ω′(G_n x))∘DG_n(x) = ω″(G_n x)∘DG_n(x), because γ ↦ γ∘T is linear. Apply (CL) with both approximations equal to (G_n) with O₀, Λ, to the form ω″ and to the sequences η_n(ω″) and a·η_n(ω) + b·η_n(ω′) (both eventually compatible with (G_n, ω″) near spt X): X(a·η_n(ω) + b·η_n(ω′)) − X(η_n(ω″)) → 0. As X is linear, X(a·η_n(ω) + b·η_n(ω′)) = a·X(η_n(ω)) + b·X(η_n(ω′)) → a·S₀(ω) + b·S₀(ω′) (step 6). Hence X(η_n(ω″)) → a·S₀(ω) + b·S₀(ω′), and by uniqueness of limits S₀(a·ω + b·ω′) = a·S₀(ω) + b·S₀(ω′). In particular (a = b = 1, and b = 0 with ω′ := ω) S₀ is additive and homogeneous.
8. (Bound, current and mass.) Passing to the limit in step 4 (the closed condition |·| ≤ const is preserved under limits) gives |S₀(ω)| ≤ (Λ^k·M(X).toReal)·C whenever |ω(y)| ≤ C for all y. The sibling current_criterion (P := m′, n := k, U := univ, T₀ := S₀, B := Λ^k·M(X).toReal) gives S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) with S(ω) = S₀(ω) for every ω and M(S) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Λ^k·M(X).toReal). Since Λ^k ≥ 0 and M(X) < ∞, ENNReal.ofReal(Λ^k·M(X).toReal) = ENNReal.ofReal(Λ^k)·ENNReal.ofReal(M(X).toReal) = (Λ : ℝ≥0∞)^k·M(X) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). This is the mass conjunct M(S) ≤ Λ^k·M(X).
9. (LipPF(X, G, S).) Let (G′_n) be C^∞, O′ open with spt X ⊆ O′, L′ ∈ ℝ with eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G′_n x‖ ≤ L′ on O′, G′_n → G uniformly on O′, ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and (η′_n) eventually compatible with (G′_n, ω) near spt X. (CL) applied to (G_n) with O₀, Λ and the sequence η_n(ω), and to (G′_n) with O′, L′ and the sequence η′_n, gives X(η′_n) − X(η_n(ω)) → 0; and X(η_n(ω)) → S₀(ω) = S(ω) by step 6. Hence X(η′_n) = (X(η′_n) − X(η_n(ω))) + X(η_n(ω)) → S(ω).
10. (Uniqueness.) Let S′ ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) satisfy LipPF(X, G, S′). Applying it to (G_n) with O₀, Λ, to ω and to η_n(ω) (eventually compatible by step 3) gives X(η_n(ω)) → S′(ω); by step 6 also X(η_n(ω)) → S(ω). By uniqueness of limits in ℝ, S′(ω) = S(ω) for every ω, so S′ = S (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
11. (Support.) Let y₀ ∉ closure(G(spt X)). The closure is closed, so there is ρ > 0 such that ball(y₀, 3ρ) is disjoint from closure(G(spt X)); then dist(G(x), y₀) ≥ 3ρ for every x ∈ spt X. Let W := ball(y₀, ρ): W is open, closure W ⊆ closedBall(y₀, ρ) is compact, and closure W ⊆ univ. Let ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and put K := tsupport ω (closed). For z ∈ K and x ∈ spt X: dist(G(x), z) ≥ dist(G(x), y₀) − dist(z, y₀) > 3ρ − ρ = 2ρ. By uniform convergence on O₀ ⊇ spt X, for all large n we have dist(G(x), G_n(x)) < ρ for every x ∈ spt X, hence dist(G_n(x), z) > ρ > 0 for all z ∈ K, i.e. G_n(x) ∉ K. For such n, N_n := G_n⁻¹(ℝ^{m′} ∖ K) is open (G_n is continuous and K is closed) and contains spt X, and for x ∈ N_n we have ω(G_n x) = 0 (as G_n x ∉ tsupport ω), so ω(G_n x)∘DG_n(x) = 0, which is the value at x of the zero form. Thus the zero sequence η′_n := 0 is eventually compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, and step 9 (with the approximation (G_n), O₀, Λ) gives X(0) = 0 → S(ω), so S(ω) = 0. Hence S vanishes on W (S(ω) = 0 for every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W), so W belongs to the family of open sets whose union is zeroRegion(S), and y₀ ∈ W ⊆ zeroRegion(S), i.e. y₀ ∉ spt S = univ ∖ zeroRegion(S). Therefore spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)).
12. (Conclusion.) S satisfies LipPF(X, G, S) (step 9), uniqueness among currents with this property (step 10), M(S) ≤ Λ^k·M(X) (step 8) and spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)) (step 11), which is the conclusion of (I). ∎

Source: Step 7 of the supplied proof of lipschitz_pushforward, including fact (dP) (d commutes with pull-back for compatible forms), which is proved inline in step 5. Assume (RS) and (I), and fix m, m′, j, X ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m), G, Λ, r, S with M(X) < ∞, M(∂X) < ∞, r > 0, G Λ-Lipschitz on (spt X)_r and proper on spt X, and LipPF(X, G, S).

1. (∂X satisfies the hypotheses of (I) with k := j.) By part (1) of the reused support_lemmas (U := univ), spt ∂X ⊆ spt X; supports of currents on univ are closed. M(∂X) < ∞ by assumption. HEq condition: let j′ ∈ ℕ and Y ∈ D_{j′+1}(ℝ^m) with j = j′ + 1 and HEq Y ∂X; substituting j = j′ + 1, HEq between terms of the same type gives Y = ∂X, so ∂Y = ∂∂X = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary), and M(0) = 0 < ∞, because the zero current takes the value 0 on every form, so every element of the supremum defining its mass is ENNReal.ofReal 0 = 0. Since (spt ∂X)_r ⊆ (spt X)_r (thickening is monotone in the set), G is Λ-Lipschitz on (spt ∂X)_r. G is proper on spt ∂X: for compact K, G⁻¹(K) ∩ spt ∂X = (G⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X) ∩ spt ∂X is the intersection of a compact set with a closed set.
2. (The push-forward of ∂X.) By (I) applied to ∂X (with k := j and the same G, Λ, r) there is S_∂ ∈ D_j(ℝ^{m′}) with LipPF(∂X, G, S_∂) (the first conjunct of (I)).
3. (Reference sequence and compatible forms.) Fix φ ∈ D^j(ℝ^{m′}). (RS) with F := spt X gives C^∞ maps G_n with ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ Λ for all n and x ∈ O₀ := (spt X)_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on O₀, and G_n proper on spt X for all large n. O₀ is open and spt ∂X ⊆ spt X ⊆ O₀ (r/2 > 0), so (G_n) with O₀ and Λ is an admissible approximating sequence both in LipPF(X, G, ·) and in LipPF(∂X, G, ·). For each n such that G_n is proper on spt X, the reused compatible_form (P := m, Q := m′, U := V := univ, A := spt X, f := G_n, ω := φ) gives θ_n ∈ D^j(ℝ^m) and an open N_n ⊇ spt X with θ_n(x) = φ(G_n x).compContinuousLinearMap (DG_n(x)) for all x ∈ N_n; for the other n put θ_n := 0. So for all large n, θ_n is compatible with (G_n, φ) near spt X, hence also near spt ∂X (same N_n).
4. (Limit along ∂X.) LipPF(∂X, G, S_∂) applied to (G_n), O₀, Λ, φ and (θ_n) gives ∂X(θ_n) → S_∂(φ).
5. ((dP): d commutes with the pull-back.) Let n be as in step 3 and x ∈ N_n. Let p_n(x′) := φ(G_n x′).compContinuousLinearMap (DG_n(x′)). N_n is an open neighbourhood of x on which θ_n = p_n, so θ_n and p_n agree near x and their exterior derivatives at x agree (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq). Since φ is C^∞ (hence differentiable at G_n(x)) and G_n is C^∞ (hence ContDiffAt of order ≥ 2 at x), Mathlib's extDeriv_pullback gives (extDeriv p_n)(x) = (extDeriv φ)(G_n x).compContinuousLinearMap (DG_n(x)). The test forms dθ_n := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ j θ_n and dφ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ j φ have underlying forms extDeriv θ_n and extDeriv φ. Hence dθ_n(x) = (dφ)(G_n x).compContinuousLinearMap (DG_n(x)) for x ∈ N_n, i.e. dθ_n is compatible with (G_n, dφ) near spt X for all large n.
6. (Limit along X.) LipPF(X, G, S) applied to (G_n), O₀, Λ, the form dφ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m′}) and the sequence (dθ_n) gives X(dθ_n) → S(dφ), and S(dφ) = ∂S(φ) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply).
7. (Identification.) ∂X(θ_n) = X(dθ_n) for every n (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply). By steps 4 and 6 and uniqueness of limits in ℝ, S_∂(φ) = ∂S(φ). Since φ was arbitrary, S_∂ = ∂S (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and step 2 gives LipPF(∂X, G, ∂S), which is the conclusion of (II). ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂X satisfies the hypotheses of (I): finite mass, ∂∂X = 0 for the HEq condition, spt ∂X ⊆ spt X (support_lemmas) gives the Lipschitz and properness hypotheses.
(I) gives S_∂ with LipPF(∂X, G, S_∂).
With the reference sequence of (RS) for F := spt X and compatible θ_n (compatible_form), ∂X(θ_n) → S_∂(φ).
(dP) via extDeriv_eq on the open set N_n and extDeriv_pullback: dθ_n is compatible with (G_n, dφ), so ∂X(θ_n) = X(dθ_n) → S(dφ) = ∂S(φ).
Hence S_∂ = ∂S and LipPF(∂X, G, ∂S).

For X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} and S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}), LipPF(X, G, S) means: for every sequence (G_n) of C^∞ maps ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, every open O ⊇ spt X and every L ∈ ℝ such that eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O, and G_n → G uniformly on O, and for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and every sequence (η_n) in D^k(ℝ^m) such that eventually η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, the sequence X(η_n) converges to S(ω). Assume (RS): for all m, m′ ∈ ℕ, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, r ∈ ℝ and F ⊆ ℝ^m such that r > 0, F is closed, G is Λ-Lipschitz on F_r and G is proper on F, there are C^∞ maps G_n : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (n ∈ ℕ) with ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ Λ for all n and all x ∈ F_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on F_{r/2}, and G_n proper on F for all sufficiently large n (this is the conclusion of the sibling reference_sequence). Then the following holds: (III) For all m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, X, X₁, X₂ ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, r > 0, S, S₁, S₂ ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) and a, a₁ ∈ ℝ such that G is Λ-Lipschitz on thickening r (spt X ∪ spt X₁), G⁻¹(K) ∩ (spt X ∪ spt X₁) is compact for every compact K, X₂(ω) = a·X(ω) + a₁·X₁(ω) for all ω, and LipPF(X, G, S), LipPF(X₁, G, S₁), LipPF(X₂, G, S₂): S₂(ω) = a·S(ω) + a₁·S₁(ω) for all ω.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 8 of the supplied proof of lipschitz_pushforward. Assume (RS) and fix m, m′, k, X, X₁, X₂, G, Λ, r, S, S₁, S₂, a, a₁ as in (III).

1. (The common support.) F := spt X ∪ spt X₁ is closed (supports of currents on univ are closed). By part (3) of the reused support_lemmas (U := univ, which is open; Z := X₂, Z₁ := X, Z₂ := X₁, coefficients a, a₁; hypothesis X₂(ω) = a·X(ω) + a₁·X₁(ω) for all ω), spt X₂ ⊆ F.
2. (Reference sequence.) (RS) with this F (r > 0, F closed, G Λ-Lipschitz on F_r and proper on F) gives C^∞ maps G_n with ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ Λ for all n and x ∈ O_F := F_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on O_F, and G_n proper on F for all large n. O_F is open and contains F ⊇ spt X, spt X₁, spt X₂ (r/2 > 0), so (G_n) with O_F and Λ is an admissible approximating sequence in LipPF(X, G, ·), LipPF(X₁, G, ·) and LipPF(X₂, G, ·) (the derivative bound holds for every n, in particular eventually).
3. (Compatible forms.) Fix ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}). For each n such that G_n is proper on F, the reused compatible_form (P := m, Q := m′, U := V := univ, A := F, f := G_n) gives η_n ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) and an open N_n ⊇ F with η_n(x) = ω(G_n x).compContinuousLinearMap (DG_n(x)) for x ∈ N_n; for the other n put η_n := 0. So for all large n, η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near F, hence near each of spt X, spt X₁ and spt X₂ (same N_n).
4. (Limits.) LipPF(X, G, S), LipPF(X₁, G, S₁) and LipPF(X₂, G, S₂), applied to (G_n), O_F, Λ, ω and (η_n), give X(η_n) → S(ω), X₁(η_n) → S₁(ω) and X₂(η_n) → S₂(ω). Since X₂(η_n) = a·X(η_n) + a₁·X₁(η_n) for every n, also X₂(η_n) → a·S(ω) + a₁·S₁(ω). By uniqueness of limits in ℝ, S₂(ω) = a·S(ω) + a₁·S₁(ω). As ω was arbitrary, this is the conclusion of (III). ∎
proof_key_steps: F := spt X ∪ spt X₁ is closed and contains spt X₂ (support_lemmas (3)).
(RS) for F gives one approximating sequence admissible for X, X₁ and X₂, and compatible_form gives one eventually compatible η_n near F.
